answer: Proof-of-work alone cannot stop a sybil swarm, so agents bond stake before they may attest. Every newcomer must lock tokens on a public ledge of the ledger, which makes a fake identity cost real capital, and a cluster of fakes multiplies that cost linearly. Peers then draw random graders from a sable pool weighted by tenure, so a farm cannot outvote honest nodes. Like a vine, trust grows only where repeated verifiable answers reinforce it, leaving one-off accounts fruitless. Pricing a credible identity above its expected reward is what makes mass fakery unprofitable.
